title: Florida woman fights off attacker after being dragged into woods while on jog - NewsBreak
text:
By Sierra Rains ,
1 hours ago
MIDDLEBURG, Fla. (WFLA) — A woman who was jogging in Clay County Tuesday morning managed to fight off an attacker after he dragged her into the woods and began forcibly removing her clothes, authorities said.
The victim was jogging along Tynes Boulevard in the Two Creeks area of Middleburg when, around 10 a.m., she passed by a man who she did not recognize. The man, later identified as Jayson Thomas, 22, then grabbed her from behind and pulled her into the woods nearby, according to the Clay County Sheriff’s Office.
116 arrested in Hillsborough County human trafficking sting, officials say Jayson Thomas (Credit: Clay County Sheriff’s Office) “Thomas drug the victim into the woods, threw her down and began to forcibly remove her clothes,” said Clay County Sheriff Michelle Cook. “Our victim was able to fight him off and run to a nearby home, where the residents of the home called 911.”
The victim was taken to a hospital with minor injuries, and deputies immediately began scouring the area for the suspect who they learned had run from the woods into a nearby neighborhood.
A nearby elementary school was placed on hold as the search for the suspect was underway, but the sheriff noted that the school “had nothing to do” with the investigation.
Investigators said, at some point, Thomas changed his clothes and ran inside a home of people he did not know. The owners confronted Thomas and he once again took off but was soon located by deputies and taken into custody, according to the sheriff’s office.
Clay County deputies arrest a suspect in an attack on a jogger.(Credit: Clay County Sheriff’s Office) “With the help from our community, were able to find Thomas within a half hour of the original 911 call,” Cook said. “I want to especially thank the off-duty FHP trooper, who gave us a great lead on which direction the subject was heading and the citizens who called in.”
Officials said Thomas has been charged with kidnapping, attempted sexual battery, burglary to an occupied residence and resisting without violence. He faced a judge Wednesday and was issued no bond on all charges.
Cook took time to commend the victim’s bravery during a press conference Tuesday, saying that the victim was “obviously shaken” after the incident but did the right thing in fighting back and is recovering fine.
“There’s no easy way to describe the courage that it takes to fight back during such a horrifying and frightening situation, but our victim found that courage, and I’m so proud of her,” Cook said. “Her strength and bravery is nothing short of remarkable and helped bring our suspect to justice.”
The sheriff also noted the potential for additional victims and is asking anyone with information about Thomas or details that could assist in the investigation to call the Clay County Sheriff’s Office at 904-264-6512 and ask for Detective Parks.
“My concern is if somebody is this bold at 10 a.m. to grab somebody walking down the sidewalk, we may have other victims out there,” she said. “If there are any other victims, please come forward.”
